title: Week 1 — Exam Secrets Nobody Tells You (ADM-201)
tweets:
I scored 92% on the Salesforce Admin exam (ADM-201) on my second attempt.

Nobody told me I was studying the WRONG way first.

Here's what changed everything 🧵

#Salesforce #ADM201

I spent 8 weeks following Trailhead modules in order (like everyone tells you to).

Failed with 58%.

Then I realized: The exam doesn't test chronologically.
It tests specific topics 80% of the time.
Most courses bury those in later modules.

The exam obsesses over:
• Permission Set groups
• Flow vs Process Builder edge cases
• SharingRule vs OrgWideSharingDefault
• LoginFlow vs Validation Rule timing

These 4 topics? 30-40% of the exam.

But modules hide them everywhere.

#SalesforceAdmin

What changed (2nd attempt):
1. Took practice exam FIRST (didn't study, just tested)
2. Found my weak spots
3. Studied ONLY those weak spots using docs
4. Retook practice exam (targeted those areas again)

Total study time: 3 weeks instead of 8.

Attempt 1: Failed (58%)
Attempt 2: Passed (92%)

The difference wasn't working harder.
It was having a study METHOD.

I used TrailblazePrep practice questions mapped to topics.
Changed everything.

title: Week 3 — Salesforce Flow Tips
tweets:
flow is a huge chunk of app builder and real admin work. six things i wish someone had yelled at me earlier 🧵

#Salesforce #SalesforceFlow

process builder → flow migration still shows up. know what you'd rebuild as flow.

#SalesforceFlow #AppBuilder

record-triggered: before vs after save actually matters. i got burned once on related updates. worth labbing.

#SalesforceFlow #SalesforceAdmin

subflows beat one 80-node monster. easier debug, reuse, and it's the right answer when you duplicated logic everywhere.

#SalesforceFlow #AppBuilder

fault paths: without them you're blind when flow dml fails. 2 min to add. hours saved at 9pm. @SteveMoForce yells about this too.

#SalesforceFlow #Trailblazer

debug: step through. doesn't fire. check entry conditions first then actually read the debug output.

#SalesforceFlow #SalesforceAdmin

one interview = one run. variables don't persist. free flow + app builder qs on our site. link next.

#AppBuilder #SalesforceCertified

engagementTweets.text:
before-save vs after-save still trips people up. system vs user context shows up in weird sharing edge cases.

#SalesforceFlow #SalesforceAdmin

biggest flow you've shipped. mine was embarrassing before subflows. still not proud of v1.

#SalesforceFlow #Trailblazer

_updatedEngagement.text: Flow thing nobody mentions: before-save flows run in system context so sharing rules don't apply. after-save flows run in user context. that difference affects which records they can see and update. it's subtle and it shows up.
